label: paragraph_title
text: "ANTI-FOREIGN."

label: text
text: STRANGE REPORT FROM CANTON

label: text
text: DEMONSTRATION TO-MORROW?

label: text
text: Moves to organise an anti-Christian and anti-foreign demonstration in Canton to-morrow are said to be disfavoured by the Provinciall Government.

label: text
text: The demonstration, or procession—about which word has reached the Canton authorities—may be the predecessor of something promised for Christmas for which a certain section had planned things on a fairly extensive scale.

label: text
text: It may also be that the preparations for to-morrow—and there certainly have been signs that the organisation is ready—may be more anti-Christian, essentially, than anti-foreign.

label: text
text: At any rate the Canton Government is rumoured to be striving to restrict the demonstrators to the city which is taken to mean giving the Shakee and adjacent parts of the Bund a wide berth.

label: text
text: Some of the more conservative of the Kuomintang politicians are even said to be opposed to the idea of a procession along the waterfront, this report emanating from a statement that steps have been taken to be ready for emergencies.

label: paragraph_title
text: “ IOLANTHE.”

label: text
text: NO PERFORMANCE THIS EVENING

label: text
text: There is no performance of "Iolanthe" this evening as erroneously announced in the morning papers. A matinee will be given to-morrow evening. Further performances take place on Thurs- day, Friday and Saturday evening.

label: paragraph_title
text: LOCAL WEDDINGS

label: paragraph_title
text: WALL—MCGREGOR

label: text
text: Dr. Austin Darley Wall of Shanghai and Miss Margaret Alice McGregor, who arrived from Home by the s.s. "Antenor," were married at St. John's Cathedral on Friday afternoon last.

label: text
text:
The bride was given away by Dr. C. H. Brangwin, port medical officer of Swatow who has just returned from a year's leave.
Surg.-Lt.-Com. Brown, H.M.S.
Hawkins," was the best man

label: text
text: FOSTER-TURNER—RADLEY.

label: text
text: St. John's Cathedral was the scene of a pretty wedding yesterday when Mr. Frederick Wentworth Foster-Turner and Miss Rosina Lily Radley were joined in marriage.

label: text
text: The "bridegroom is well known in Hongkong as an architect and is the son of Mr. and Mrs. J. Foster-Turner of Bush Hill Park, N., and the bride the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. R. Radley, of Cross Park, Pilton, North Devon. She arrived in the Colony during the week-end.

label: text
text: The bride, who was given away by Mr. S. Hamer, was beautifully dressed in white crepe satin, trimmed with Brussels lace, and wore a Brussels lace veil with white heather and a wreath of orange blossoms. Her bouquet was of white roses and chrysanthemums.

label: text
text: The bridesmaid was Miss Gladys Brock, who wore a charming dress of pale pink- crepe de chine trimmed with silk lace and hat to match. She carried a bouquet of pink roses and chrysanthemums.

label: text
text: Mr. S. Feltham acted as best man to the bridegroom. The Rev. T. B. Powell, M.A., officiated and Mr. F. Mason was at the organ.

label: text
text: After the ceremony a reception was held at the residence of Mr. S. Hamer, 10 Ventris Road, where many friends of the bride and bridegroom gathered to offer good wishes.

label: text
text: Later, Mr. and Mrs. Foster-Turner left for Cheung Chau, where the honeymoon is to be spent. The bride's going away dress was of-tan crepe-de-chine with lace to tone and velvet ribbon, her hat being of brown Bangkok straw with flowered wreath.

label: text
text: FORTHCOMING LEGAL BATTLE

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Sydney, Dec. 14.

label: text
text: Messrs. Walsh and Johannsen have applied for writs claiming £20,000 each from the Government alleging wrongful arrest and imprisonment.

label: text
text: Mrs. Walsh and Mrs. Johannsen are also claiming £5,000 for loss of their husbands' services.

label: text
text: It may be recalled that Mrs Walsh was formerly Miss Adela Pankhurst, the militant. suf-fragette.

label: text
text: This is an echo of the recent seamen's strike in Australia when the Government felt compelled to use drastic measures of arrest, imprisonment and deportation. Messrs. Walsh and Johannsen were arrested, but subsequently released on an order of the Supreme Court of Australia, and are now claiming against the Government.

label: text
text: Mrs. Walsh, was formerly Miss Adela Pankhurst, of the Pankhurst trio who led the suffragette movement some years ago. When the movement succeeded, the Pankhurst family withdrew from it. The other sister is engaged in religious work.

label: paragraph_title
text: INDIA'S CONDITION.

label: paragraph_title
text: VICEROY'S "ROSY PICTURE."

label: text
text: COMMERCIAL ENERGY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Calcutta, Dec. 14.

label: text
text: A rosy picture of India's economic condition was painted by Lord Reading in an exhaustive address to the Indian Chambers of Commerce.

label: text
text: He recalled the depressing conditions of 1921 and the adverse trade balance, 800,000,000 rupees. The political atmosphere was

label: text
text:
trade balance, 800,000,000 rupees.
The political atmosphere was heavily charged and though there was still room for improvement last year's overseas trade had reached the record figure 650,000,-000 rupees.

label: text
text: The Budget, which showed a deficit of 200,000,000 rupees in 1921 was made into a surplus last year.

label: text
text: The military expenditure last year was 560,000,000 rupees compared with 760,000,000 in 1921.

label: text
text: In regard to labour legislation, the Viceroy mentioned the Bill submitted to the Assembly to encourage and protect a healthy trade union organisation.

label: text
text: He attributed the improved outlook to the grit and energy of the commercial community; also the improvement in the political situation which engendered a feeling of stability and continuity.

label: paragraph_title
text:
FRENCH FINANCE
AN OMINOUS SYMPTOM

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Páris, Dec. 14.

label: text
text: An ominous symptom in the politic and financial situation is revealed by the Finance Committee of the Chamber referring back the Finance Bills dealing with further taxation and the establishing of a Sinking Fund.

label: text
text: [An earlier message states:—

label: text
text: M. Loucheur's financial proposals is taking active form in various parts of the country, business groups regiotering protests. A Carcassonne a solemn pledge was taken by all local tradespeople to refuse to pay taxes if the pro

label: text
text: posals were adopted, while the Nimes Commercial Union has decided on a two hours strike as a protest.

label: text
text: The fall of the franc is causing a steady rise in the prices of commodities. Figures published by the General Statistics Service show a rise of nine per cent. in wholesale prices in France in October and November compared to a fall in Britain, Germany, Sweden, Czech, Slovakia, Switzerland.

label: paragraph_title
text: SORDID CASE

label: text
text: HAYLEY MORRIS ON TRIAL.

label: text
text: COUNSEL AND JURY'S DUTY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, Dec. 14.

label: text
text: Sir E. Marshall Hall, in opening the prosecution, said: Morris was a merchant engaged in Chinese trade.

label: text
text: The woman prisoner. Roberts, had been a domestic servant and also a shop assistant, but when arrested was acting house keeper to Morris.

label: text
text: Detailing the charges, counsel said Roberts had not merely conspired to procure girls, but did her utmost to get them to do what she knew Morris's wanted them do.

label: text
text: Sir Marshall Hall told how the police began to make enquiries after the girl, in the absence of the prisoners, telephoned her friends in London.

label: text
text: The roads were searched and the girl was found crouching in a ditch, completely exhausted, and taken to her friends.

label: text
text: The evidence of other girls was obtained.

label: text
text: There were three cases of girls under 16; other cases of girls above 16, besides girls who resisted and escaped from harm.

label: text
text: He concluded by asking the jury, if they convicted the accused "of a sordid, abominable offence," not to let fear or favour deter them from recording a proper verdict. A number of girls then testified.

label: paragraph_title
text: Girl's Admission.

label: text
text: The Hayley Morris case has been adjourned until tomorrow. The Judge directed that both the accused should remain in custody.

label: text
text: The most interesting witness was the female prisoner's sister who said her father was dead. She had been in the service of the female prisoner who left home when her father died.

label: text
text: The witness was not aware of her whereabouts until last Christmas when she telephoned witness to come to Pippingford Park.

label: text
text: She stayed, two nights, and a fortnight later she took her there by train, buying her a few clothes.

label: text
text: Her third visit lasted six weeks. Nothing happened till the third visit. She had not told her sister of it.

label: text
text:
Another sister was also there.
The witness said she told
Morris before the alleged incident, that her age was 14.

label: text
text:
Cross-examined, witness said she never told anyone about the matter till the police saw her.
The police helped her to remember what happened.

label: paragraph_title
text: Judge's Opinion.

label: text
text:
An earlier cable message states: —The trial of Hayley Morriss and his wife opened sensationally at Lewes Assizes. The male defendant appeared in charge of a warder and the woman walked briskly from a local hotel, smiling as Press photographers snapped her. Both pleaded not guilty.
The Judge declined to hear evidence of the woman's condition. Replying to counsel's plea that she was not fit to stand a long trial, he said: "My opinion is that already there has been a deliberate attempt to deserve the Court, and I am not sure there has not been something worse, namely, an attempt to interfere with the course of justice." He declined to hear her counsel further.

label: text
text: Washington, Dec. 15.

label: text
text: The Republican Senator Fish has toged a resolution in the House to prohibit the concentration of foreign elements in its own settlements.

label: text
text: Sentator Fish asserts the resolution is due to Mussolini's suggestion that Italian centres should be tested in the United States.

label: paragraph_title
text: HONGKONG AND THE BOYCOTT.

label: text
text: FURTHER ASSISTANCE POSSIBLE

label: text
text: (Reulect's Service.)

label: text
text: London, Dec. 14.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, Mr. A. Spoor asked for information of the purposes of the loan of £3,000,000 to the Hongkong Government; and whether the Government had taken steps to terminate the boycott of British trade in Hongkong.

label: text
text: Mr. Ormsby Gore replied that the Governor had applied in September for a loan of the amount mentioned for the purpose of restoring confidence and financing trade.

label: text
text: · The loan had saved the Colony at a serious moment.

label: text
text: It is possible that if the boycott continues and trade worsens, further assistance may have to be considered next year.

label: paragraph_title
text: IQUOR SMUGGLING.

label: text
text: Reuben's American Service.

label: text
text: Washington, Dec. 15.

label: text
text: Senator Jones, of Washington, has introduced a resolution, backed by the Administration, providing for the appropriation of $9,000,000 to construct ten coast-guard cutters to suppress liquor smuggling.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL AND OIL.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Agreements for a concession of 45 years for coal and oil fields in North Saghalien to Japanese firms recommended by the Japanese Government, were signed to-day under the Japan, Soviet and Peking Treaty.

label: paragraph_title
text: CIVLL WAR.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: According to messages from Japanese sources in China, Wu Pei-fu is reported to be marching on Shanghai.

label: text
text: Tientsin's trenches held by General Feng Yu-hsiang, were stormed at the point of the bayonet and his forces expelled from Yangtsun by General Li Ching-lin who is an ally of Chang Tso-lin.

label: paragraph_title
text: GERMANY.

label: text
text: (Heuter's Scroice.)

label: paragraph_title
text: London: Dec. 15.

label: text
text: The “Daily Telegraph” diplomatic correspondent states that Mr. Parker Gilbert, Agent-General for Reparations, accompanied by Mr. Norman, Governor of the Bank of England, have gone to the United States presumably in connection with the problem of further credits for Germany, and, certain aspects of the eventual raising of a second Dawes Loan.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: TELEPHONE COMPANY'S SHARE LIST.

label: text
text: OVERSUBSCRIPTION POSSIBLE.

label: text
text: Judging from the very large number of applicants at the cashier's department of the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank to-day, the end of the day may quite possibly see the over-subscription of the subscription list for the 250,000 shares in the Hongkong Telephone Company which opened this morning.

label: text
text: The majority of the applicants appeared to be Chinese.

label: text
text: If the list is oversubscribed, applicants will have shares allotted in proportion to the oversubscription, with certain preferences for bona fide residents and telephone subscribers. It all-depend on the amount subscribed to-day whether the list will remain open further or for how long.

label: text
text: With the applications being forwarded to the offices of the Company, this evening, the staff will probably work until late in sorting them out and to-morrow it should be possible to estimate the total amount of the applications.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry this morning of Mr. A. L. Terry, acting secretary, a “China Mail” representative was informed that at the time it was impossible to estimate the number of shares actually applied for, but there were indications that the issue was being very favourably received by the public.

label: paragraph_title
text: A STOLEN BANGLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUSPICION LEADS TO ARREST.

label: text
text: A HEAVY SENTENCE

label: text
text: Sentience of six months $ ^{1} $ hard labour and 15 strokes of the birch was imposed by Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning on a Chinese charged with larceny of a gold-mounted bangle from a little girl.

label: text
text: The complainant, a Chinese married woman, stated in evidence that she was at a market stall in Eastern Street yesterday afternoon along with her family of three small children. Defendant was observed to be petting one of the girls, whom he enticed some distance away, when he stole the bangle. The theft was noticed when the girl came back to the complainant, but the defendant had then disappeared.

label: text
text: The suspicions of a Chinese detective were aroused when he met a man on the pavement who suddenly stopped in his walk, stared at him, and walked again. A little further down the road the detective was informed of the theft, and in a search the "suspect" was caught in a side street. The stolen bangle was found in his pocket. These facts were given by the detective in his evidence.

label: text
text: His Worship imposed sentence as stated above.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: CYCLIST INJURED.

label: text
text: A Chinese youth riding a push bicycle at Praya East, near Triangle Street, late last night, lost control of his machine and steered into a motor car. The rider was thrown out of the cycle and injured, the machine being also badly smashed.

label: text
text: Finding that the cyclist was rather seriously injured, the driver of the car promptly took him to the Government Civil Hospital.

label: text
text: Inadvertence through unacquaintance with custom was the explanation offered by Mr. H. S. Fitzroy on behalf of the South China Restaurant for non-compliance with requirements with regard to share allotment filing. The time for filing allotments was extended until December 22 at the Supreme Court this morning.
